# ZeroClaw Docs

> Documentation for the ZeroClaw personal AI assistant.

This index lists every page of the ZeroClaw Docs site. The full text of all pages is available in one file at https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/llms-full.txt. The HTML site is at https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/.

## Introduction

- [Introduction](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/introduction.html): Personal AI assistant you own, written in Rust.

## Philosophy

- [Philosophy](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/philosophy/index.html): ZeroClaw is built on four opinions, in priority order.
- [You own it](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/philosophy/you-own-it.html): The binary runs on your machine, your VPS, or your SBC. Your API keys live in your config file. Your conversation history lives in your database. No telemetry, no cloud tenancy, no license server. If…
- [Security-first, with escape hatches](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/philosophy/security-first.html): Local-first doesn't mean consequence-free. An agent that can execute shell commands, call HTTP endpoints, and write files is a privileged process. The default autonomy level is supervised:…
- [Minimal: in binary size, dependencies, and surface area](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/philosophy/minimal.html): ZeroClaw is written in Rust and optimised for a small binary and fast startup. The microkernel split (RFC #5574) factors functionality behind feature flags so you only ship what you use: the…
- [Provider-agnostic](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/philosophy/provider-agnostic.html): The agent's brain is pluggable. Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, Bedrock, Gemini, Azure, OpenRouter, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Groq, Mistral, xAI, and ~20 others) work out of the box. Per-agent…
- [What this isn't](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/philosophy/what-this-isnt.html): Not a SaaS. There's no hosted version, no account system, no billing.
- [How decisions get made](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/philosophy/how-decisions-get-made.html): Substantive changes go through the RFC process: see Contributing → RFCs. An RFC labelled status:accepted is ratified and binding even while its implementation is still open; the discussion thread…

## Getting Started

- [Getting Started](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/getting-started/index.html): Start here if you are installing ZeroClaw for the first time or choosing the simplest path to a working agent.
- [Concepts](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/getting-started/concepts.html): These are the terms Quickstart and the config reference assume. Each one has a deeper page linked at the end of its definition.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/getting-started/quickstart.html): Quickstart is the guided setup that takes you from a fresh install to a working agent in one pass. It runs on three surfaces: the CLI, the zerocode terminal interface, and the web gateway. All three…
- [YOLO mode](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/getting-started/yolo.html): YOLO mode disables every safety gate ZeroClaw ships with. No approval prompts, no workspace boundary, no shell policy, no command allow/denylist, no OTP, no sandbox. The agent can run any shell…
- [Multi-model setup](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/getting-started/multi-model-setup.html): A walkthrough of the common patterns for using multiple model providers: per-agent dispatch, hint routes, cost tiering, local-first with hosted backup, non-streaming provider fallback, rate-limit…
- [zerocode](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/getting-started/zerocode.html): zerocode is ZeroClaw's terminal interface for managing configuration, chatting with agents, and monitoring your daemon. It connects over a local IPC stream, a Unix domain socket on Unix or a named…
- [Language & translations](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/getting-started/language.html): ZeroClaw's interface strings (CLI messages, command help, and the zerocode TUI) can be shown in languages other than English. English is always built in; other languages are downloaded on demand.

## zerocode

- [zerocode](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/zerocode/overview.html): zerocode is ZeroClaw's terminal interface for managing configuration, chatting with agents, and monitoring your daemon. It connects over a local IPC stream, a Unix domain socket on Unix or a named…
- [Running zerocode](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/zerocode/running.html): On the same machine as the daemon, no extra configuration is needed:
- [Config pane](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/zerocode/config.html): zerocode's Config pane is the way to configure a running ZeroClaw. Each setting has a typed control, validation, and an inline explanation of what it does, and most settings apply live without a…
- [Themes & terminal colours](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/zerocode/themes.html): zerocode ships a set of named color themes, lets each agent carry its own theme in the Code and Chat panes, and adapts its color output to what the terminal can render.
- [Remote setup (WSS)](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/zerocode/remote.html): Connect zerocode on your workstation to a daemon running on another machine (Raspberry Pi, home server, VPS, etc.).
- [Secure transport (end-to-end config)](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/zerocode/secure-transport.html): This page is the full configuration reference for connecting a client to a daemon securely, in three topologies:
- [Environment pass-through](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/zerocode/environment.html): The daemon runs as a background process and typically has a stripped-down environment. Your terminal has the full environment set up by your shell profile. There are two ways env vars reach shell…

## Installation

- [Installation](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/setup/index.html): Choose the installation path for your operating system or deployment target.
- [Linux](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/setup/linux.html): Install, update, run as a service, and uninstall, all Linux distributions.
- [macOS](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/setup/macos.html): Install, update, run as a LaunchAgent, and uninstall on macOS (Intel or Apple Silicon).
- [Windows](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/setup/windows.html): Install, update, run as a Windows scheduled task, and uninstall on Windows 10 / 11.
- [FreeBSD](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/setup/freebsd.html): ZeroClaw runs natively on FreeBSD (tested on FreeBSD 15.0-RELEASE, amd64). Two things differ from the Linux/macOS/Windows paths:
- [NixOS](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/setup/nixos.html): ZeroClaw ships a multi-instance NixOS module at `nix/module.nix`. It runs one or more agents under systemd with hardening defaults appropriate for an internet-facing process, modelled on…
- [Docker & containers](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/setup/container.html): Run ZeroClaw in Docker, Podman, Kubernetes, or any OCI runtime.
- [Service management](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/setup/service.html): ZeroClaw ships with first-class service integration for systemd (Linux), launchctl (macOS), and Task Scheduler (Windows). All three are driven by one CLI surface:
- [Platform install files](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/setup/dist-files.html): ZeroClaw ships ready-to-use packaging and service files for several platforms under `dist/`. These are operator-facing: copy them to your host instead of hand-writing package or service definitions.

## Architecture

- [Architecture](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/architecture/overview.html): ZeroClaw is a layered Rust workspace. At the top is the agent runtime; below it are pluggable providers, channels, tools, and memory; supporting crates handle config, sandboxing, and hardware.
- [Request lifecycle](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/architecture/request-lifecycle.html): What happens between "user sends a message" and "agent replies": the full path, with streaming, tool calls, and security gates annotated.
- [Channel runtime lifecycle](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/architecture/channel-runtime-lifecycle.html): Channels sit at the edge of ZeroClaw. They talk to chat platforms, webhooks, editors, and event sources, then hand normalized work to the agent runtime.
- [Tool execution lifecycle](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/architecture/tool-execution-lifecycle.html): ZeroClaw tools are capabilities the model can invoke during a turn. The tool catalog says what can be called; the execution lifecycle says how a call becomes safe, observable, cancellable, and…
- [Background work lifecycle](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/architecture/background-work-lifecycle.html): ZeroClaw has several ways to continue work after the inbound request that started it. Cron jobs, SOP runs, delegated tasks, and runtime-spawned subagents share some execution machinery, but they do…
- [Provider routing lifecycle](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/architecture/provider-routing-lifecycle.html): Provider routing begins after ZeroClaw has selected the agent that owns a turn. It covers provider-profile and model selection, retries and fallback, stream recovery, and the attribution that…
- [Crates](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/architecture/crates.html): The workspace is split into layers. Edge crates talk to the outside world; core crates orchestrate; support crates provide utilities. Each crate has its own rustdoc, see API (rustdoc).

- [Logging](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/architecture/logging.html): ZeroClaw has exactly one logging surface: the zeroclawlog::record! macro. Every emission in the workspace, agent loop activity, channel I/O, cron runs, tool calls, memory ops, session lifecycle,…
- [Runtime state and persistence](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/architecture/runtime-state-and-persistence.html): ZeroClaw has one install root, but not one monolithic "workspace database". Different state surfaces have different owners, reload behavior, and durability. Use this map when a change adds state,…
- [Memory and payload lifecycle](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/architecture/memory-payload-lifecycle.html): ZeroClaw carries several kinds of "remembered" information during a turn. They do not all have the same owner, durability, privacy boundary, or review risk.
- [Config lifecycle](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/architecture/config-lifecycle.html): Configuration is both an operator interface and a runtime contract. Treat it as state with a clear owner, not as loose settings copied into whichever subsystem needs them.
- [Generated documentation pipeline](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/architecture/generated-documentation-pipeline.html): ZeroClaw documentation combines hand-authored Markdown with references and snippets materialized from Rust types, command definitions, registries, WIT contracts, workflow files, and UI metadata. Mozilla Fluent catalogs provide application strings for the runtime and zerocode. gettext catalogs translate the mdBook…

- [Config](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/reference/config.html): ZeroClaw is configured via a TOML file. All fields are optional unless noted.

- [API (rustdoc)](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/api.html): Full rustdoc for every public type in the workspace, auto-generated from the /// comments on each type, function, and module. Use this when you need to know the exact shape of a struct, the methods…
- [Gateway HTTP API](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/gateway/api.html): The gateway exposes a REST surface alongside the local CLI. Anything that can be set with zeroclaw config get/set/list/init/migrate is also reachable via HTTP, so the dashboard, third-party tooling,…
- [A2A agent discovery](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/gateway/a2a-discovery.html): This deployment can publish its agents so another deployment, or any HTTP client, can find them and call them. A2A is the protocol for one agent to reach another agent, the way a person reaches a bot…

## Agents

- [Agents](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/agents/overview.html): Agents are the star of a ZeroClaw deployment. Everything else in this book, the providers, the channels, the security profiles, the skills, the memory, exists so that an agent can use it. This…
- [Anatomy of an agent](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/agents/anatomy.html): An agent is configured as a single agents.<alias> block. Every field is either a reference to something configured elsewhere or a per-agent override. The table below is generated from the config…
- [Filesystem components](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/agents/filesystem.html): The relational half of an agent points at config; the on-disk half lives under the install root. The layout is organized by scope, not one flat tree: instance-wide state, cross-agent shared…
- [Running agents](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/agents/operating.html): Because there is no privileged "the agent," every command that drives an agent names which one. Agents coexist; you address one by its alias.
- [Agent portability](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/agents/portability.html): An agent is not a file. It is a config entry that references providers, profiles, bundles, and MCP servers, plus a workspace directory on disk. Moving one to another install means moving both halves,…
- [Delegation & SubAgents](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/agents/delegation.html): A SubAgent is an ephemeral child run spawned by a parent agent that inherits the parent's identity by default: same agent alias, same SecurityPolicy, same memory allowlist, same configured model…
- [Runtime internals](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/agents/internals.html): This page is the architecture-depth companion to the rest of the Agents section: how the runtime enforces per-agent permissions, scopes memory, and attributes logs. For configuring and running…
- [History management](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/agents/history-management.html): The runtime keeps conversation history for each agent session and sends a provider-facing working history to the model. Two complementary limits operate on different representations:

## Model Providers

- [Provider catalog](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/providers/catalog.html): Every model-provider family ZeroClaw ships with. For each: config shape, notes on auth and endpoint behavior, and the slot key to use under providers.models.<type>.<alias>.
- [Configuration](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/providers/configuration.html): Every model provider lives at providers.models.<type>.<alias>. <type> is a canonical family slot (see the Catalog for every slot with its endpoint). <alias> is your operator-assigned instance name,…
- [Streaming](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/providers/streaming.html): Streaming is capability-driven. Providers that implement the streaming methods and return supportsstreaming() == true can emit token deltas; other providers use the non-streaming response path. The…
- [Routing](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/providers/routing.html): ZeroClaw uses routing for two different decisions:
- [Custom providers](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/providers/custom.html): Three ways to add a provider ZeroClaw doesn't ship with:
- [OpenAI Codex (subscription)](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/providers/openai-codex-subscription.html): Run an agent on the openai slot, paid through a ChatGPT subscription instead of metered OPENAIAPIKEY billing. ## Channels & Integrations

- [Channels & Integrations](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/overview.html): A channel is a messaging surface the agent talks through. One ZeroClaw instance can bind multiple channels simultaneously: the same agent can answer in Discord, Telegram, email, and over the REST…
- [Peer Groups](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/peer-groups.html): A peer group declares who an agent accepts inbound messages from on a channel, and which other agents it can exchange messages with there. It is the inbound gate for chat channels and the routing…
- [Matrix](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/matrix.html): Run ZeroClaw in Matrix rooms, including end-to-end encrypted (E2EE) rooms.
- [Telegram](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/telegram.html): Run a ZeroClaw agent as a Telegram bot over long polling. No public URL or webhook is required. This guide starts with the runtime wiring, then walks from bot creation through the first authorized…
- [Discord](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/discord.html): Run your ZeroClaw agent as a Discord bot. This guide walks you through it click by click, no prior bot experience needed. By the end you'll have a bot sitting in your server that replies when people…
- [Slack](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/slack.html): Run your ZeroClaw agent as a Slack bot. This guide walks you through it step by step. By the end you'll have a bot in your workspace that answers when people message it or @-mention it.
- [Mattermost](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/mattermost.html): REST v4 polling and WebSocket client. By default the bot polls channels every 3 seconds for new posts; set listenmode = "websocket" for near-real-time event delivery over a persistent WebSocket…
- [LINE](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/line.html): ZeroClaw supports LINE via the Messaging API, receiving messages through an embedded webhook server and replying via the Reply API (with Push API fallback when the reply token has expired).
- [Nextcloud Talk](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/nextcloud-talk.html): Nextcloud Talk integration via the Talk Bot webhook protocol. Self-hosted, federated, and E2E-capable: another sovereign-communication option alongside Matrix and Mattermost.
- [Signal](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/signal.html): ZeroClaw's Signal channel talks to a running signal-cli HTTP daemon. Signal does not provide an official bot API, so ZeroClaw connects to signal-cli over local HTTP and lets signal-cli own the Signal…
- [WhatsApp](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/whatsapp.html): ZeroClaw supports two WhatsApp backends under the same channels.whatsapp config family:
- [Other chat platforms](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/chat-others.html): Channels with working integrations but not yet pulled out into dedicated guides. Each is feature-gated; enable the matching channel-<name> feature at build time.
- [Social (Bluesky, Nostr, Twitter, Reddit)](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/social.html): Broadcast / social-feed integrations. These differ from chat channels in two ways: messages are typically public, and the agent often acts as a poster rather than a bidirectional responder.
- [Email](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/email.html): Two email channels depending on how you want inbound messages delivered.
- [Voice & telephony](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/voice.html): Real-time voice input and output. Four channels cover the matrix: inbound calls, local microphone wake, outbound speech synthesis, and SIP-grade real-time conversation.
- [Webhooks](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/webhook.html): The webhook channel is a generic inbound/outbound HTTP adapter. It runs its own embedded HTTP server on a port you choose, accepts JSON-shaped messages, hands them to the agent, and (optionally)…
- [MQTT](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/mqtt.html): The mqtt channel subscribes to topics on an MQTT broker and feeds each message into the agent loop or the SOP engine. It is gated by the channel-mqtt build feature.
- [AMQP](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/amqp.html): The amqp channel consumes messages from an AMQP 0-9-1 broker (RabbitMQ and compatible). Each delivery can drive the agent loop, start a SOP run, or both, selected per alias by the dispatch field.
- [Filesystem](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/filesystem.html): The filesystem channel watches one or more paths and feeds each change into the agent loop or the SOP engine. It is gated by the channel-filesystem build feature (default on).
- [ZEGA AI (external prototype)](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/integrations/zega-ai.html): --- type: reference status: proposed last-reviewed: 2026-08-05 relates-to:
- [Git (GitHub / Gitea / Forgejo)](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/git.html): Converse with the agent through a git forge's issue and pull-request comments, and surface repository events, including PR lifecycle, review comments, CI outcomes, and releases, through a per-event…
- [Creating a GitHub App](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/git-github-app.html): The Git channel with provider = "github" authenticates as a GitHub App, not as a user. The app has its own bot identity (your-appbot), its own permissions, and works on every repository it is…
- [Creating a Gitea / Forgejo token (Codeberg)](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/git-gitea-forgejo.html): The Git channel with provider = "gitea" or provider = "forgejo" authenticates with a personal access token against the instance's Gitea-compatible REST API, and replies as the token owner. Both…
- [ACP (Agent Client Protocol)](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/channels/acp.html): ACP is a JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol over stdio that lets editors and IDEs drive a running ZeroClaw agent as a session host. Newline-delimited JSON, lightweight, streamable, easy to wire to a subprocess.

## Tools & Extensibility

- [Tools & Extensibility](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/tools/overview.html): Tools are the agent's hands. A tool is a capability the model can invoke mid-conversation, run a shell command, fetch an HTTP URL, open a browser, write a file, read a sensor. Every tool call is…
- [MCP (Model Context Protocol)](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/tools/mcp.html): ZeroClaw is an MCP client: it connects to external Model Context Protocol servers and exposes their tools to the agent. Each MCP tool is namespaced as <server><tool> (for example filesystemreadfile),…
- [Browser automation](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/tools/browser.html): This guide covers setting up browser automation capabilities in ZeroClaw, including both headless automation and GUI access via VNC.
- [Relationship memory](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/tools/relationship-memory.html): Relationship memory is the opt-in graph side of the knowledge tool. Use it when an agent needs to remember how things connect, not only which text snippet matches a query.
- [Using relationship memory from skills](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/tools/relationship-memory-skill-template.html): Use this template when you want a skill to tell an agent when and how to capture workflow, capability, and steward-role relationships with the knowledge tool. It keeps the graph as an operator-facing…
- [Skills](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/tools/skills.html): Skills are reusable instructions and optional tool definitions that ZeroClaw can load into an agent session. Use them for repeatable workflows such as code review checklists, deployment runbooks,…
- [Skill bundles](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/tools/skill-bundles.html): A skill bundle is the one plugin kind that ships no WebAssembly at all. It is a directory of markdown skills, packaged and distributed through the plugin machinery: same manifest, same discovery,…
- [Python skills](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/tools/python-skills.html): ZeroClaw can run Python skills, but realistic Python work usually needs one of two explicit deployment choices:

## Security & Autonomy

- [Security & Autonomy](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/security/overview.html): An agent that can execute shell commands, open URLs, and write files is a privileged process. ZeroClaw's security model sits on top of every tool call and every channel message, gating what the agent…
- [The security model](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/security/model.html): ZeroClaw's security model gates what the agent is allowed to do at runtime. There are six layers. From outer to inner:
- [Authentication & principals](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/security/authentication.html): Every RPC connection to the daemon binds a principal during the initialize handshake, and every method call is checked against the grants the current configuration assigns that principal. This page…
- [Autonomy levels](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/security/autonomy.html): Autonomy is a per-agent setting that lives on a named risk profile: risk_profiles.<alias>.level. Each agent references one risk profile via agents.<alias>.riskprofile = "<profile-alias>". Three…
- [Sandboxing](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/security/sandboxing.html): The runtime can wrap tool invocations in an OS-level sandbox that restricts filesystem access to the workspace and removes access to the parent process's secrets. This is distinct from the autonomy…
- [Tool receipts](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/security/tool-receipts.html): Tool receipts are cryptographic proofs that a successful tool result came from the runtime. When receipts are enabled, successful tool executions receive an HMAC-SHA256 digest over the call and its…

## Operations & Deployment

- [Operations & Deployment](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/ops/overview.html): How to run ZeroClaw in production. The surface is intentionally small: one binary, one config file, and one install root with a handful of runtime stores. Most "operations" is "systemd and journald".
- [Service & daemon](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/ops/service.html): This page is the operations-side companion to Setup → Service management; that page covers installing and uninstalling the service. This page covers running it: tuning, resource limits, graceful…
- [Logs & observability](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/ops/observability.html): Every event ZeroClaw emits flows through one crate: zeroclaw-log. The crate owns the on-disk JSONL schema, the in-process broadcast stream the dashboard reads, the optional typed Observer bridge, the…
- [Cost tracking](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/ops/cost-tracking.html): ZeroClaw records every token-bearing model call to an append-only ledger, including calls whose pricing is only partially available. It attributes spend to the originating agent, enforces daily /…
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/ops/troubleshooting.html): Common failure modes, in the order you're likely to encounter them.
- [Network deployment](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/ops/network-deployment.html): Deploying ZeroClaw so it can receive inbound traffic: gateway exposure, webhook channels, tunnels, and LAN-only vs. public-facing configurations. Raspberry Pis and other home-network hosts are…
- [Eval harness](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/ops/eval-harness.html): The eval harness (zeroclaw eval run, crate crates/zeroclaw-eval) runs agent evaluation cases (JSON trace fixtures) through the real agent loop and grades each run against declarative expectations. It…

## Hardware & Boards

- [Hardware & Boards](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/hardware/index.html): ZeroClaw's hardware subsystem lets the agent control microcontrollers, SBCs, and peripherals directly. Enable with --features hardware.
- [Hardware subsystem](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/hardware/subsystem.html): ZeroClaw's hardware subsystem lets the agent control microcontrollers, SBCs, and peripherals directly. Enable with --features hardware.
- [Adding boards & tools](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/hardware/adding-boards-and-tools.html): This guide explains how to add new hardware boards and custom tools to ZeroClaw.
- [Peripherals design](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/hardware/hardware-peripherals-design.html): ZeroClaw enables microcontrollers (MCUs) and Single Board Computers (SBCs) to dynamically interpret natural language commands, generate hardware-specific code, and execute peripheral interactions in…
- [Arduino Uno Q](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/hardware/arduino-uno-q-setup.html): Run ZeroClaw on the Arduino Uno Q's Linux side. Telegram works over WiFi; GPIO control uses the Bridge (requires a minimal App Lab app).
- [STM32 Nucleo](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/hardware/nucleo-setup.html): Run ZeroClaw on your Mac or Linux host. Connect a Nucleo-F401RE via USB. Control GPIO (LED, pins) via Telegram or CLI.
- [Android](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/hardware/android-setup.html): ZeroClaw can publish an experimental prebuilt binary for Android devices.
- [Raspberry Pi](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/hardware/raspberry-pi-setup.html): This guide covers installing and running ZeroClaw on Raspberry Pi.

## Standard Operating Procedures

- [Standard Operating Procedures](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/index.html): SOPs are deterministic procedures executed by the SopEngine. They provide explicit trigger matching, approval gates, and auditable run state.
- [How SOPs run](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/how-it-works.html): Run state and audit history are separate surfaces. See Background work lifecycle for lifecycle ownership, cancellation, and restart semantics.
- [Syntax](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/syntax.html): SOP definitions are loaded from subdirectories under sopsdir, which is unset by default, so runtime SOP execution is off until an operator opts in. Set sopsdir to a directory to enable it: a relative…
- [Decision models](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/decision-models.html): A decision model answers typed questions about an event instead of generating text. An SOP can ask one, after its trigger matches and before a run starts:
- [Cookbook](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/cookbook.html): Practical SOP templates in the runtime-supported SOP.toml + SOP.md format.
- [SOP Fan-In](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/fan-in/overview.html): A fan-in is an external event source that starts SOP runs. Each source delivers events to the SOP engine through dispatchsopevent, which matches every event against every loaded SOP's triggers and…
- [MQTT](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/fan-in/mqtt.html): MQTT messages can start SOP runs. The MQTT listener subscribes to the broker, builds a SOP event per message, and dispatches it to the engine. This path is gated by the channel-mqtt build feature.
- [Filesystem](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/fan-in/filesystem.html): Filesystem changes can start SOP runs. The watcher monitors one or more paths with a recursive notify watcher, debounces and settles each change, builds a SOP event per change, and dispatches it to…
- [AMQP](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/fan-in/amqp.html): AMQP deliveries can start SOP runs. When an alias runs in a SOP dispatch mode, the AMQP consumer lifts each delivery into a SOP event (the routing key becomes the event topic, the message body…
- [Channel](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/fan-in/channel.html): Inbound messages on an agent-loop channel (Telegram, Discord, Slack, and the other conversational channels) can start SOP runs. When a loaded SOP wants channel events, the orchestrator lifts each…
- [Git](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/fan-in/git.html): Git forge events can start SOP runs. When an event type is routed to sop in the channel's event table, the Git channel lifts the normalized forge event into a SOP event (the topic is…
- [Manual](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/fan-in/manual.html): A manual trigger starts a run from inside an agent turn, not from an external event. The agent calls the sopexecute tool, naming the SOP to run. There is no listener and no event source to configure;…
- [Webhook](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/fan-in/webhook.html): The gateway exposes two authenticated HTTP entry points for webhook-triggered SOPs:
- [Cron](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/fan-in/cron.html): A cron trigger fires on a time window described by a cron expression. Invalid expressions fail closed during parsing and cache build.
- [Peripheral](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/fan-in/peripheral.html): A peripheral signal is matched exactly against board/signal.
- [Calendar](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/fan-in/calendar.html): A calendar trigger matches against a calendar event topic, scoped to a calendar source and optionally to specific calendar IDs.
- [Observability](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/observability.html): This page covers where SOP execution evidence is stored and how to inspect it.
- [Worked Example](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/sop/example.html): stagehand is a production ZeroClaw bot. It watches the upstream release feed, bumps a StageX package, builds it, verifies it reproduces by digest, pushes the change, opens a draft pull request, and…

- [Writing a channel plugin](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/plugins/writing-a-channel-plugin.html): A channel plugin is a messaging-platform integration: it delivers the agent's responses to a platform and surfaces the platform's messages to the agent. It is the most involved plugin kind, because a…
- [Writing a memory plugin](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/plugins/writing-a-memory-plugin.html): A memory plugin is a storage backend: it persists what the agent remembers and answers recall queries. It is the most data-model-heavy plugin kind. Where a tool has one function and a channel has a…
- [Distributing plugins](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/plugins/distributing-plugins.html): You built a plugin; now it needs to leave your machine without asking the people who install it to trust you blindly. ZeroClaw's distribution story has two independent layers: Ed25519 manifest…
- [Migrating to typed config](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/plugins/migrating-to-typed-config.html): Typed instance config is a breaking change for every pre-1.0 plugin that reads operator configuration. This page is the migration artifact for plugin authors and operators: what breaks, why, and the…
- [Building the docs locally](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/developing/building-docs.html): The docs site you're reading is published from docs/book/. You can build the same site on your own machine, useful for offline reading, previewing edits before opening a PR, or developing…
- [Building the web dashboard](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/developing/web.html): The web dashboard at web/ is a Vite + React + TypeScript app. Its TypeScript API client is generated from the gateway's runtime OpenAPI spec, not hand-written.

## Contributing

- [Contributing](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/contributing/index.html): Start here before opening issues, proposing architecture changes, or submitting pull requests.
- [How to contribute](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/contributing/how-to.html): We accept code, docs, bug reports, and feedback from anyone willing to file them clearly. This page covers the mechanics: how to get a change in, what we look for in review, and what to expect after…
- [Coding agent guidelines](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/contributing/agent-guidelines.html): The repository-root AGENTS.md is the compact, always-loaded contract for AI coding assistants. This page provides details that are useful for some tasks but should not consume every session's prompt…
- [Architecture and contribution map](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/contributing/architecture-map.html): Use this page when a change is larger than a typo and you are not sure which architecture, foundation, contributor, or maintainer documents apply.
- [RFC process](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/contributing/rfcs.html): An RFC records a durable project-level decision before implementation. The process exists to surface design trade-offs, give maintainers and contributors a chance to push back early, and leave a…
- [Communication](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/contributing/communication.html): Where to ask questions, file bugs, propose features, and reach the team.
- [Privacy & PII discipline](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/contributing/privacy.html): ZeroClaw artifacts are public, git history, releases, fixtures, snapshots, the docs book, every rendered locale. Anything you commit ships with the project forever. Treat privacy as a merge gate, not…
- [Testing](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/contributing/testing.html): ZeroClaw uses a five-level testing taxonomy backed by filesystem layout. Each level has a different boundary and a different cost; pick the lowest level that proves what you need to prove.
- [User-boundary proof](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/contributing/user-boundary-proof.html): A user-visible behavior claim is proved by reaching the outermost production boundary affected by the claim and checking the result a user observes. Unit, component, and compile checks remain useful,…
- [Agent-policy parity](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/contributing/agent-policy-parity-harness.html): An agent's policy - which tools it may call, when it must ask for approval, its runtime budgets, its memory scope, and its skills - must be enforced identically no matter which code path assembles…
- [PR review protocol](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/contributing/pr-review-protocol.html): This is the procedure followed when reviewing a pull request in zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw. It's loaded by the github-pr-review-session skill and read by human reviewers, it's authoritative for both.
- [Multi-agent setup](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/contributing/multi-agent-setup.html): This is the operator-side companion to the Agents section. Follow it to add a second agent to an install, configure cross-agent memory access, and put both agents in a peer group on the same channel.
- [Contributor License Agreement](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/contributing/cla.html): By submitting a contribution (pull request, patch, issue with code, or any other form of code submission) to the ZeroClaw repository, you agree to the terms below. No separate signature is required…

- [CI & Actions](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/maintainers/ci-and-actions.html): Every workflow lives in .github/workflows/. The sections below group them by trigger: automatic on git events, or maintainer-invoked/advisory workflows via workflowdispatch and schedules.
- [Claude Code Skills](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/maintainers/skills.html): The repo ships a set of Claude Code skills under .claude/skills/ that automate the heavier parts of the maintainer workflow: PR reviews, issue triage, squash-merging, changelog generation, and more.
- [PR workflow](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/maintainers/pr-workflow.html): The maintainer-side governance contract for PRs targeting master. Branch-protection settings, the DoR/DoD readiness contracts, and the failure-recovery protocol live here. Day-to-day reviewing lives…
- [Reviewer playbook](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/maintainers/reviewer-playbook.html): The operating model for reviewing PRs and triaging issues. Sized to keep review quality high under heavy volume; routes by risk so high-stakes paths get the attention they need without dragging every…
- [Labels](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/maintainers/labels.html): Single reference for every label used on PRs and issues. Sources of truth:
- [Superseding PRs](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/maintainers/superseding.html): When a maintainer-authored PR replaces a contributor's open PR, attribution and process discipline keep the contributor relationship healthy. This page is the rulebook.
- [Release runbook](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/maintainers/release-runbook.html): Last verified against the v0.8.2 release cycle.
- [Release artifact verification](https://docs.zeroclaw.com/master/en/maintainers/release-verification.html): ZeroClaw uses GitHub artifact attestations as the canonical provenance mechanism for downloadable release assets. Each successful attestation records the asset digest, source commit, and release…
